strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages the results with `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT) and `offset`, and returns `{ total, items }`. It refuses a limit or offset that isn't a whole number, and a limit below 1, with a 400. The tests start the real app with createApp() on an OS-chosen port and check the responses against the real catalogue (PRODUCTS).
inScope: GET /products: q filtering, listing without q, limit/offset paging, total count, the limit cap, 400 validation
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
The search box UI (no UI exists in this repo)
assumptions: The cap is the code's exported MAX_LIMIT (50 today). The README says 100, so I asked as Q1. The tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT instead of hard-coding them.

The tests run the real app in-process, nothing faked, on port 0, the same way test/products.test.js does. The expected values come from filtering the imported PRODUCTS, so the tests don't reimplement the app's logic: each one asserts concrete ids or names for the data it queries.
Results are ordered by id, as the README says, and pages are contiguous slices of that order.
A negative offset or limit (e.g. -1) counts as 'not a whole number', and the code refuses it with 400.
openQuestions: Q1: is the limit cap 100 (README) or 50 (code MAX_LIMIT)?

risks.description: A case-sensitive or prefix-only match would miss products whose name contains the query
risks.mitigation: TC1 sends a mixed-case query that matches the middle of names and asserts the exact set of names returned

risks.description: total could report the page size instead of the number of matches
risks.mitigation: TC3 and TC4 check total against the full match count while the page is smaller

risks.description: Without a working cap, a huge limit could return the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC5 asks for limit=1000 and expects exactly MAX_LIMIT items

risks.description: Bad paging input could return 200 or 500 instead of 400
risks.mitigation: TC6–TC8 cover a non-integer, a non-numeric and a negative value, and a limit of 0

acceptanceCriteria.text: q returns exactly the products whose name contains q, case-insensitively; without q every product is listed (subject to paging)
Results are paged with limit and offset, the response's total is the number of all matches, and a limit above the maximum is capped to the maximum
A limit or offset that is not a whole number, or a limit below 1, is refused with 400

testCases.title: matches products whose name contains q in any case
preconditions: App listening on an ephemeral port
testCases.expected: 200; total is 30, and items are exactly the Teapot and Tea strainer products, by id; every item's name contains 'tea' when lower-cased
testCases.testData: q=tEA (matches 'Teapot n' and 'Tea strainer n', 15 of each)
testCases.rationale: Core search behaviour: mixed case, and a match that isn't only at the start of the full name

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200; total equals PRODUCTS.length (120); items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products by id
testCases.rationale: Without q, everything is listed, with the default page size

testCases.title: returns the page at offset with limit items and the total of all matches
testCases.expected: 200; total 15; items are Kettle 11 to Kettle 14 (ids 81, 89, 97, 105)
testCases.rationale: Paging applies to the filtered matches, and total counts them all

testCases.title: returns no items but the full total when offset is past the last match
testCases.rationale: Boundary: an offset at the end of the matches

testCases.title: caps a large limit at the maximum page size
testCases.expected: 200; items are exactly the first MAX_LIMIT products; total 120

testCases.title: refuses a limit that is not a whole number with 400
refuses an offset that is not a whole number with 400

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services. The tests start the app in-process with createApp().listen(0).
